label: thm:perron/root
title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $A$ be a positive square matrix. Then $A$ has a positive real eigenvalue. Its largest eigenvalue $\lambda_0>0$ is simple and satisfies $|\lambda_0|>|\lambda|$ for every other eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A$. Moreover, all $n$-row minors of the matrix $\lambda_0 I-A$ are positive.
		\label{thm:perron/root}
head: environment

label: thm:frobenius/theorem/for/irreducible/matrices
title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $A$ be a non-zero irreducible matrix. Then the largest positive eigenvalue $\lambda_0$ is simple and $|\lambda_0|\geq|\lambda|$ for every other eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A$. Moreover, all $n$-row minors of the matrix $\lambda_0 I-A$ are positive.
		\label{thm:frobenius/theorem/for/irreducible/matrices}
head: environment
name: Frobenius Theorem

title: Theorem
body_md: For an irreducible matrix $A$, primitivity is equivalent to aperiodicity.

title: Definition
body_md:
A real algebraic integer \(\lambda>1\) is called a \emph{Perron number}\index{number!Perron} if every Galois conjugate \(\lambda'\neq \lambda\) satisfies
		\[
		|\lambda'|<\lambda .
		\]
head: environment

label: thm:lind
title: Theorem
body_md:
Given any Perron number $\lambda$,  there exists an aperiodic non-negative integral matrix which admits $\lambda$ as its dominant eigenvalue. 
		\label{thm:lind}
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md: The entropy of $f : I \to I $, denoted $h(f)$, is $\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{\log(c_{n})}{n}$.
head: environment

label: thm:existence/of/uniform/expander
title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $f: I \to I$ be a continuous, piecewise-monotone map with a finite lap number and positive topological entropy $h(f) > 0$. Then $f$ is topologically semiconjugate to a piecewise linear map $F: I \to I$ of constant absolute slope, such that 
		\[
		|F'(x)| = \lambda = e^{h(f)} > 1
		\]
		wherever the derivative is defined. The map $F$ is called a \emph{uniform $\lambda$-expander} \index{uniform expander}, and its slope directly recovers the entropy via $h(f) = h(F) = \log \lambda$.
		\label{thm:existence/of/uniform/expander}
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $f:I\to I$ be a continuous self-map of an interval $I $. A point $c\in I$ is called a \emph{critical point}\index{point!critical} of $f$ if $c$ is a local extremum point of $f$, that is, if $c$ admits an open neighbourhood in which $f(c)$ is a local maximum or minimum value. The \emph{critical set}\index{set!critical} of $f$ is the set of all local extrema:
		\[
		\operatorname{Crit}(f) := \{\, c \in I \mid c \ \text{is a critical point of} \ f \,\}.
		\]		
		The \emph{post-critical set}\index{set!post-critical} of $f$ is
		\[
		P(f)\;:=\;\overline{\bigcup_{n\geq 1} f^{n}\bigl(\operatorname{Crit}(f)\bigr)},
		\]
		where the overline denotes closure in $I$. 
		The map $f$ is called \emph{post-critically finite} (\emph{PCF})\index{map!post-critically finite} if $P(f)$ is a finite subset of $I$.

title: Remark
body_md: This construction can immediately be used to construct expanders for \emph{weak Perron} integers, which are defined as those real algebraic integers \(\lambda\)  for which \(\lambda \ge |\sigma(\lambda)|\) for all embeddings \(\sigma\). Indeed, in such a case all conjugates of $\lambda$ is an element of the closed disk of radius $|\lambda|$. Those that are on the boundary must be of the form $\zeta \lambda$ for some root of unity $\zeta$, i.e. $|\zeta| = 1$. Choose an integer $k$ so that for every such conjugate $\zeta^{k} = 1$. Then, $\lambda^{k}$ is Perron. The preceding construction leads to a \(\lambda^k\)-expander. Then the implant method can be used to yield a uniform \(\lambda\)-expander.

title: Definition
body_md:
A \emph{finite system}\index{curve system!finite} of simple closed curves on \(S\) is a finite set
		\[
		\mathcal C=\{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k\}
		\]
		where each \(\gamma_i\) is a simple closed curve on \(S\). The word \emph{finite} means that only finitely many isotopy classes of curves are involved.
head: environment
name: Finite system

title: Definition
body_md:
The system \(\mathcal C\) is called \emph{disjoint}\index{curve system!disjoint} if the curves can be chosen so that
		\[
		\gamma_i\cap \gamma_j=\varnothing
		\qquad\text{for all } i\neq j.
		\]
		Equivalently, the curves are represented by pairwise disjoint embedded circles on the surface.
head: environment
name: Disjoint

title: Definition
body_md: A simple closed curve \(\gamma\subset S\) is called \emph{essential}\index{curve!essential} if it is not null-homotopic and not homotopic into a boundary component or into a puncture. Equivalently, \(\gamma\) is essential if it does not bound a disk, a once-punctured disk, or an annulus whose other boundary component is a boundary component of \(S\).
head: environment
name: Essential

title: Definition
body_md: Two essential simple closed curves \(\gamma_1,\gamma_2\subset S\) are called \emph{parallel} if they are isotopic, or equivalently if they cobound an embedded annulus in \(S\). A system \(\mathcal C\) is called \emph{non-parallel} if no two distinct components of \(\mathcal C\) are parallel.
head: environment
name: Non-parallel

title: Definition
body_md:
A \emph{train track}\index{train track} \(\tau\) on a compact smooth surface \(S\) is an embedded multigraph, that is, a finite graph embedded in \(S\) in which multiple edges between the same pair of vertices and loops are allowed, satisfying the following conditions:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item Each vertex $v$ (called a \emph{switch}) is assigned a unique tangent line in $T_v S$. The edges (called \emph{branches}) incident to $v$ are tangent to this line. The edges are separated into two sets: those entering from the left, $E_{in}(v)$, and those leaving from the right, $E_{out}(v)$.
			\item For every connected component $U$ of $S \setminus \tau$, the completion of $U$ with respect to a path metric has a negative generalized Euler characteristic, defined by
			\[
			\chi'(U) = \chi(U) - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i} c_i < 0,
			\]
			where $c_i$ are the inward-pointing cusps on the boundary of $U$. 
		\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
A real algebraic unit \(\lambda>1\) is called a	\emph{bi-Perron unit}\index{algebraic number!bi-Perron} if every Galois conjugate \(\mu\) of \(\lambda\), (except possibly one of $\pm1/\lambda$), satisfies
		\[
			\lambda^{-1}< |\mu|< \lambda .
		\]
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md: A number $\lambda$ is the stretch factor of an end-periodic homeomorphism of a connected infinite-type surface with finitely many ends if and only if $\lambda$ is a weak Perron number.
head: environment
name: Hillen-Loving-Wu

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $G$ be a finite graph with no valence-one vertices. A continuous map $f \colon G \to G$ is a \emph{topological representative}\index{outer automorphism!topological representative of} of $\Phi \in \mathrm{Out}(F_n)$ if $f$ sends vertices to vertices, edges to paths, and induces $\Phi$ on the fundamental group. 
		Such a representative is called a \emph{graph train track map}\index{train track!graph} if for every edge $e \in E(G)$ and every integer $m \ge 1$, the path $f^m(e)$ is locally injective (i.e., it contains no non-trivial backtracking or cancellations).
head: environment

label: thm:thurston_outFn
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:thurston_outFn}
		A positive real number \(h\) occurs as the topological entropy of an ergodic graph train track representative of an outer automorphism \(\Phi\in \operatorname{Out}(F_n)\) if and only if $\lambda:=\exp(h) $ is a weak Perron number.

name: Thurston

title: Definition
body_md: Let \(\lambda\) be a Perron number. The \emph{Perron--Frobenius degree}\index{degree!Perron--Frobenius} of \(\lambda\), denoted by \(\deg_{\mathrm{PF}}(\lambda)\), is the smallest integer \(n\) for which there exists an \(n\times n\) non-negative integral primitive matrix whose spectral radius is \(\lambda\).
